deep.reconstruction:
Folio 50v carries no writing by Gauss. The only marks are faint, mirror-reversed bleed-through of the facing side, folio 50r (the 'previous page' transcription). The ghost layout matches 50r line for line.

(a) A heading and a first table of seven rows: the seven roots of x^7 - 28 x^4 + 560 = 0 ('Zug III. 180°'). The columns are the root a+bi, log10 of its modulus (n marks a negative real part), and the argument φ. A further row, the right-hand column, gives the sums (Summe -0,0000003; Σ log r = 2,7481881) and the check value log f = 2,7481880 = log10 560.

(b) The equation x^7 - 28 x^4 + 1,0654845 + 17,078968 i = 0 ('Zug III. 5°'), followed by seven root rows.

(c) Two closing rows: Summe +0,0000018 - 0,0000021 i, Σ log r = 1,2333051, Σφ = 86°25'48,674''; then log f = 1,2333051 and φ = 86°25'48,666''.

So nothing on this side is new mathematics. On 50r Gauss is following the seven roots of the trinomial-type septic x^7 - 28 x^4 + c = 0 as the constant term c moves along a path ('Zug' I-IV). Folio 51 parametrises such a path as c = 280 - sqrt(t^2 + 20000) + i t, indexed by t. The Zug III points on 50r are labelled instead by an angle (180°, 5°). At each point he computes all roots and checks two things. First, the sum of the roots is 0, since there is no x^6 term. Second, by Vieta (the product of the roots equals -c), the sum of the log moduli equals log|c| and the sum of the arguments equals arg(-c) mod 180°/360°. This is numerical root-continuation, presumably connected with his work on the fundamental theorem of algebra / root loci, but that material belongs to 50r and 51, not to 50v.
